Probably not with unaided eyes.

Although the Moon is geometrically above the horizon, it is an exceptionally thin crescent—only **1.53% illuminated**—and just **14.2° from the Sun**. At **12.9° altitude**, you would also be looking through substantial atmosphere, while the Sun is still **19° high**, producing a very bright sky. Those factors make the crescent’s contrast far too low for most ordinary observers.

A highly experienced observer might conceivably detect it with carefully aligned, optically aided viewing under excellent transparency, but naked-eye detection would be extremely unlikely. **Do not scan near the Sun with binoculars or a telescope**; wait until the Sun is fully below the horizon, though the Moon will then be very low and set soon afterward.
